correctness.rationale: Exact proof: positive atomic masses make variance strictly convex modulo constants. Tight-edge graph connectivity gives only six per-pair vertices. Replacing opposite split pairs directly or same-type split pairs by a two-point randomized mixture strictly raises expected variance, eliminating all but one split; the positive gain is (k-1)lambda(1-lambda)/k^2. The exact one-split discrete finite difference (k-2a-lambda-1)/k^2 and comparison with whole-pair cuts yield the stated formula and every equality case. Independent exact tight-tree enumeration for 2 and 3 pairs and 22 six-state checks reproduced it; finite tests are not the general proof.
